NO CABIN YET
Week 10 · Integrated Reading → Writing

Postcards Home

You're on a trip. You read an interesting story in a local magazine, and you want to tell someone at home about it. A good postcard does two things: it says what the story was about in a few of your own words, and then it says what you think. That is exactly the skill this week: summarize, then respond. It helps with Interactive Reading (finding the main idea fast) and with every DET writing task. Last week's opinion colours are back, plus a new one: violet for the summary. There's no grade, and finishing the steps counts as attending this week.

~25 min total Choose your level No sound needed One 5-minute postcard
?Not sure what to do? Tap ? How it works at the top of any stop. You will see pictures and easy steps.

STOP 01~1 min

Choose Your Cabin

Pick the level that feels right today. Your choice changes the texts you read and how much you write. Every cabin counts the same for attendance, and you can switch any time.

STOP 02~3 min

Pre-flight Briefing

DET SKILLS · INTERACTIVE READING + WRITING

In Interactive Reading, the DET asks you to find the main idea and choose the best title of a passage. In the writing tasks, you need to explain ideas in your own words and give your opinion. A postcard puts both skills together. Read this short news story and a student's postcard about it:

SummaryWhat the writer says: the main idea, in your own words. No opinion yet.
OpinionWhat you think about the story.
ReasonWhy you think it.
ExampleSomething real from your life that proves the reason.
Final wordCloses the postcard: your opinion again, or a hope or plan.

Now match each kind of sentence to its job: tap a name, then tap its job.

STOP 03~5 min

Shrink It

READING SKILL · MAIN IDEA

A postcard is small, so the whole story must fit in one sentence. Skim each story before the clock runs out (then it goes blurry!). Choose the sentence that shrinks the whole story.

TRAPWHAT'S WRONG
Too detailedOnly one small part of the story
CopiedA sentence taken straight from the text
Adds an opinionYour opinion doesn't belong in a summary
Wrong ideaThe text doesn't say this
TIPRead the first two sentences and the last sentence. Ask: who did what, and what happened?
STOP 04~4 min

In Your Own Words

WRITING SKILL · PARAPHRASE

Changing one or two words is not "your own words". A good paraphrase keeps the whole meaning but changes the words and the sentence shape. Choose the best paraphrase of each sentence.

Three ways to say it your way

Change wordsvisitors → people · fix → repair
Change the orderBecause A, B → B, so A
Change the word typedisliked → was unhappy with

Watch out for three traps: too close (only one or two words changed), changes the meaning, and leaves out an important part.

STOP 05~3 min

Writer or Me?

WRITING SKILL · SUMMARY vs RESPONSE

A student wrote a postcard about the first story in Stop 3, but the sentences got mixed up in the mail. For each sentence: is it what the writer says (summary), what I think (response), or off topic? Keep your streak going 🔥.

TIPSummary signals: The article says / According to the writer / The story explains. Response signals: I think / In my opinion / In my house / I would.
🔥 0
STOP 06~10 min

Full Flight: Write a Postcard

DET PRACTICE · READ → SUMMARIZE → RESPOND

Read a magazine article, then you have 5 minutes to write your postcard: a summary in your own words and your response. You can look back at the article while you write, but the page will show any long parts you copied.
